title: Boss: integration day
summary: Decide how every branch should land, resolve the conflicts, and build the merge engine.

steps.title: The scene
body: Friday: `feature/search` has to land before the release cut, and `feature/filters` was built on top of it.
`main` moved on during the week, so you expect trouble.
You work in a real repository each time: first look before you leap (what will the merge bring, and where will it
conflict?), then merge and resolve, then rescue the stacked branch after the team squash-merged its base.

steps.prompt: `feature/search` has 7 commits: *wip*, *wip*, *fix test*, *Add search*, *wip*, *Add filters*, *fix lint*. Only you have pushed to it, and review has not started. Best move?
options: `git rebase -i main`: squash and fixup into 2 clean commits (*Add search*, *Add filters*), then `git push --force-with-lease`
Merge it as is; history is history
steps.explain: Private branch, not reviewed yet: rewriting is safe and makes review and future `blame` far easier.

steps.title: Look before you merge
prompt: In `~/shop`, before you merge anything, find out what merging `feature/search` into `main` would do:
1. Save the subjects of the commits it would bring in, one per line, in `~/answers/brings.txt`.
2. Save the names of the files that would conflict, one per line, in `~/answers/conflicts.txt`.
Do it **without** starting a merge: `main` and the working tree must stay exactly as they are. `git merge-tree --write-tree main feature/search` does a merge in memory and prints the conflicts.

checks.name: brings.txt lists the commits the merge brings in
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && diff <(sed '/^$/d' ~/answers/brings.txt | sort) <(git log --format=%s main..feature/search | sort)
checks.fail: `~/answers/brings.txt` should hold the subjects of the commits on `feature/search` that `main` does not have. `git log --format=%s main..feature/search` prints them.

checks.name: conflicts.txt lists the conflicting files
checks.fail: `~/answers/conflicts.txt` should name each file that would conflict, one per line. `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main feature/search` lists them after the tree id.

checks.name: main and the working tree are untouched
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse main)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/main-start)" && ! test -f .git/MERGE_HEAD && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
checks.fail: `main` moved or a merge is in progress. `git merge --abort` (or Reset scenario) gets you back.

hints: `A..B` means "reachable from B but not from A": the commits a merge of B into A brings.
`git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main feature/search` prints a tree id, then the conflicted files, then messages. Its exit code is 1 when there are conflicts.
`git log --format=%s main..feature/search > ~/answers/brings.txt`, and write the two file names into `conflicts.txt` (with `printf` or by cutting them out of the merge-tree output).
solution: git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main feature/search | sed -n '2,/^$/p' | sed '/^$/d' > ~/answers/conflicts.txt
steps.explain: `git merge-tree --write-tree` (Git 2.38+) is the same merge the hosting platforms run to say "this branch has conflicts", without touching your working tree. `git log main..feature/search` and `git diff main...feature/search` (three dots: since the merge base) are the two views of a pull request: its commits and its change.

steps.title: Merge and resolve two conflicts
prompt: Now merge `feature/search` into `main` in `~/shop` and resolve both conflicts as the team agreed:
- `src/Search.cs`: keep **main's** limit (`20`, for mobile) and the **branch's** sort (`"relevance"`).
- `src/Menu.cs`: the menu gets all four items: `{ "Home", "Search", "Cart", "Help" }`.
Finish the merge with Git's default message.

checks.name: the merge of feature/search is committed
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && ! test -f .git/MERGE_HEAD && test "$(git rev-parse HEAD^2 2>/dev/null)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/search-tip)" && test "$(git branch --show-current)" = main
checks.fail: `main` should end in a merge commit whose second parent is `feature/search`.

checks.name: Search.cs: limit 20, relevance sort
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && grep -q 'int Limit = 20;' src/Search.cs && grep -q 'Sort = "relevance"' src/Search.cs && ! grep -qE '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)' src/Search.cs
checks.fail: `src/Search.cs` should keep `Limit = 20` from main and `Sort = "relevance"` from the branch, without markers.

checks.name: Menu.cs has all four items
checks.fail: `src/Menu.cs` should list Home, Search, Cart and Help.

hints: `git merge feature/search`, then `git status` lists both files under *Unmerged paths*.
Small files are quickest to rewrite: `printf '%s\n' 'class Search' '{' '    int Limit = 20;' '    string Sort = "relevance";' '}' > src/Search.cs`.
Same for `src/Menu.cs`, then `git add src/Search.cs src/Menu.cs` and `git commit --no-edit`.
solution: printf '%s\n' 'class Search' '{' '    int Limit = 20;' '    string Sort = "relevance";' '}' > src/Search.cs
steps.explain: Real resolutions are decisions, not mechanics: here someone had to know that the mobile limit wins and the new sort stays. That is why the person who resolves the conflict should understand both sides, and why tests (and a look at `git diff HEAD^1` afterwards) matter before pushing.

steps.title: Rescue the stacked branch with rebase --onto
prompt: The team **squash-merged** `feature/search` into `main` as one commit, `Search: relevance sort and menu entry (#42)`. Your `feature/filters` was branched from `feature/search`, so it still carries the three old search commits underneath your two filter commits.
A plain `git rebase main` would try to replay those old search commits and conflict. Move **only** your two filter commits onto `main`.
When you are done, `git log --oneline main..feature/filters` shows `Add brand filter` and `Add price filter`, nothing else.

checks.name: feature/filters is main plus the two filter commits
checks.expectOutput:
Add brand filter
Add price filter
checks.fail: `git log --format=%s main..feature/filters` should print only the two filter commits.

checks.name: it sits on top of the squashed commit
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/squashed)" feature/filters && grep -q 'brand' <(git show feature/filters:src/Filters.cs) && grep -q relevance <(git show feature/filters:src/Search.cs)
checks.fail: `feature/filters` should be based on the new `main` (with the squash commit) and still have both filters.

checks.name: no rebase is in progress
checks.fail: A rebase is still running or files are left over. `git rebase --abort` starts over.

hints: `git log --oneline --graph --all` shows where the filter commits start: on top of `Sort search by relevance` (the tip of `feature/search`).
`git rebase --onto <new base> <old base> <branch>` replays the commits after the old base only.
steps.explain: Squash merges make a new commit, so Git cannot tell that the old search commits are already in `main`. `--onto` names the cut explicitly: everything after `feature/search`, replayed on `main`. For whole stacks of branches, `git rebase --update-refs` moves every branch in the stack in one go (module 7). Afterwards `git push --force-with-lease` updates the pull request.
